title: SLO deviation investigation worklog
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the running investigation into a recent SLO deviation for 99th-percentile generation latency observed on 2025-09-30 across hosted-api-prod in us-west1. Goal: capture hypotheses, reproduce locally, run structured bisect experiments, and record canary vs baseline comparison artifacts so we have a clear mitigation path and a repeatable post-mortem.

Top-level symptoms observed:
- 99p generation latency jumped from ~420ms to ~760ms for 2048-token seqs (default model variant) between 2025-09-29 22:00 UTC and 2025-09-30 03:00 UTC.
- Error rate unchanged (<0.05%), throughput (rps) slightly lower due to client backoff.
- CPU utilization on routing nodes normal; GPU utilization on a subset of pods spiked and then plateaued.
- Canary equipped with KV cache priming did not show the same delta.

Guiding questions to answer:
1) Is this a code/regression, infra change, or workload shift?
2) Is the regression constrained to a model variant / quantization profile / kernel path?
3) Can we reproduce deterministically with recorded traces and synthetic load?
4) What fast mitigations (fallback model, routing change, scale-up) are safe to apply?

Initial data sources used:
- Grafana dashboard: Production / model-latency / 99p-generation (panel id: 2109)
- Flamegraphs from perf agent (s3://redwood-perf/trace-2025-09-30/)
- KV cache hit/miss metrics: serving.kv_cache.{hits,misses}
- Canary comparison snapshots: canary-run-2025-09-30T01:00Z.json
- Sampled traces: trace IDs saved in linked_artifacts above

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: New runtime kernel selection path introduced a slower kernel for certain token-lengths after PR #3421 was merged. (High priority)
- H2: Spotty KVCACHE eviction pattern after configuration tweak increased cold cache penalty for long requests. (Medium)
- H3: Autoscaler downscale / pod churn created transient GPU warmup issues for some shards. (Low)
- H4: External traffic pattern changed (burst of long prompts), exposing an untested tail case in batching. (Medium)

Quick repro checklist (local/lab):
- Pull exact model and runtime commit: git checkout tags/serving-runtime@2025-09-29-rc1 and serving-models@v1.12.
- Use reproduced sample trace input set (s3://redwood-perf/repro/long-prompts-2025-09-30/) with the same batching configuration as prod (batcher.max_tokens=4096, batch.timeout_ms=10).
- Run dockerized runtime with same kernel selection flags: RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=auto, QUANT_PROFILE=fp16.
- Enable perf collection: PERF_SAMPLER=1, and capture nvprof snapshots.
- Compare latency histograms using the snippet below (run in repo/tools):
  python tools/compare_histograms.py --baseline fixtures/baseline-hist.json --candidate output/hist.json --quantiles 50,90,95,99

Bisect experiment plan (parallelizable across hypotheses):
- Code regression bisect: run binary search across commits affecting kernel_selection and scheduler. Use perf harness that executes same 10k synthetic requests and compare 99p. Command: git bisect start -- bad=HEAD -- good=commit@2025-09-20; git bisect run ./ci/perf_bisect.sh
- Config delta bisect: rollback runtime flags one-at-a-time (RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT, BATCHER_TIMEOUT_MS, KVCACHE_EVICTION_WINDOW) in a canary pool and run 1-hour smoke. Document which flag reverts change via canary tag.
- Infra bisect (non-destructive): recreate pod churn in lab by scaling replicas down/up and varying GPU types (a100-vs-a10) to reproduce the GPU-spike pattern.

Canary vs baseline comparison checklist (what to capture each run):
- Full 99/99.9/99.99 quantiles and histogram buckets for generation latency across identical payloads.
- Profiling stack traces sampled at 1ms for 30s for hottest processes.
- GPU metrics: SM utilization, memory clock, power draw, GPU temp, PCIe bandwidth.
- KV cache metrics: hits/misses/evictions and per-key TTL distributions.
- Batching metrics: batch size distribution, waiting time distribution.
- Exact runtime flags and git SHAs.

Notable findings so far (notes from runs on 2025-10-03 to 2025-10-07):
- Reproduced 99p delta locally when enabling kernel fallback policy introduced in PR #3421 (switching off fallback removes delta).
- Flamegraph shows an extra ~90ms spent in kernel-selection glue on 2048-token sequences when fallback path triggers.
- Canary with pre-warmed KV cache did not trigger fallback; hypothesis H2 partially explains difference between canary and prod.

Actionable mitigations (short term):
- Immediately pin runtime to pre-PR-3421 behavior for affected production-serving pool (rollback flag KERNEL_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false) and monitor 1-hour rolling 99p. Owner: Liam.
- Open cherry-pick PR with targeted instrumented logging in kernel selector to capture why fallback triggers for specific shapes. Owner: Priya.
- Add a temporary rule in smart-router to route long-sequence requests to a conservative model variant that avoids fallback paths. Owner: Diego.

Longer-term follow-ups (post-incident):
- Replace synchronous kernel-selection path with async lookup to avoid blocking critical path; target Q1 2026 refactor.
- Extend canary priming to include long-tail prompt shapes used in production to avoid false negatives in canary comparisons.
- Expand perf CI to include 2048-token suite every merge on main.

Experiment results appendix (short summaries):
- Run 2025-10-04T14:00Z (candidate runtime with fallback ON): 99p=755ms, 90p=410ms. Baseline (fallback OFF): 99p=422ms, 90p=405ms.
- Run 2025-10-05T10:30Z (config revert KVCACHE window): negligible impact on 99p in isolated lab (suggests H2 not primary).
- Run 2025-10-06T03:20Z (simulated pod churn): reproduced GPU spike but latency recovered quickly; did not match production tail magnitude.

Dashboard and query snippets (for quick triage):
- Grafana panel query (promql):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_generation_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  and label_replace(sum(rate(serving_generation_latency_seconds_count[5m])) by (model, variant), "variant", "$1", "variant", "(.*)")
- KV cache dashboard query (clickhouse):
  SELECT sum(hits) as hits, sum(misses) as misses, toHour(event_time) as hr FROM serving.kvcache_metrics WHERE event_time >= now() - interval 48 hour GROUP BY hr ORDER BY hr

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did kernel selector choose fallback for long sequences only after merge? (need finer-grain logs)
- Can we design a guardrail in canary priming to emulate production cache state?
- Should we adopt a delayed rollout for kernel-selection changes that includes a perf-signoff gate?

Meetings and owner timeline:
- 2025-10-03 17:00 UTC: initial triage (notes in slack thread), decision to instrument and run bisect. Owners: Aisha, Liam.
- 2025-10-05 09:00 UTC: config revert attempt in canary succeeded (observed small improvement). Owner: Diego.
- 2025-10-07 13:00 UTC: rollback flag deployed to affected pool; monitoring shows 95% recovery for 99p. Owner: Liam.

How to read this doc and next steps for responders:
- If you are running a bisect: append results to this doc with the run id and a one-line summary.
- If you are on-call and see reoccurrence: toggle KERNEL_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false in the emergency flagboard and notify leads.
- If you are responsible for perf CI: please add the 2048-token suite and a long-sequence canary priming test case.

Appendix: useful commands and artifacts
- Reproduce locally (one-liner): ./ci/run_perf_repro.sh --input s3://redwood-perf/repro/long-prompts-2025-09-30/ --commit HEAD --collect nvprof
- Perf traces location: s3://redwood-perf/trace-2025-09-30/
- Canary snapshot: s3://redwood-canaries/canary-run-2025-09-30T01:00Z.json
- CI bisect script: repo/ci/perf_bisect.sh

Record of quick edits and notes:
- 2025-10-03: added hypothesis list and initial perf runs. (Aisha)
- 2025-10-04: bisect run started across kernel selection commits (Priya)
- 2025-10-06: temporary router rule added to divert long requests (Diego)

Decision log:
- 2025-10-07: rollback fallback behavior (KERNEL_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false) applied as immediate mitigation. Rationale: fastest way to restore 99p while we instrument. Owner: Exec approval via #eng-ops.

If anything in this doc is unclear, ping me (Aisha) or drop notes directly in the linked slack thread.
